findings.where: Title-block nav, the MMM Infra logo at top left (desktop and phone), and the hero section drawing, which is the logo's three arches under its band
findings.fault: The logo appears only in a colour version the client does not hold. The mark and the wordmark are turned white (linework) on the diazo blue, and the logo blue #0070C0 and grey #404040 appear nowhere on the page. In the hero, an amber hatch is also added inside the mark's third arch. The palette names no logo version for the blue ground, and does not declare the logo blue and grey as logo-only.
findings.who_objects: Mark would object. His logo is the one fixed part of the brand, and the brief says it stays and is never redrawn. Here he sees it in white with an amber fill he never approved. A reversed version needs his yes before a direction can be built on a ground where the full-colour logo cannot sit.

findings.where: Article page specimen (desktop and phone): body text, pull quote and lecture link over the gridded diazo-blue ground
findings.fault: The direction gives reading pages the same ground as the hero sheet: saturated diazo blue with the 20 mm grid crossing behind every line of prose. No calmer reading surface is defined for articles, so a long post is read in reversed text with lines running through it.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader working through one of Mark's longer articles. The pattern under the text tires the eye and makes the page feel busy, which Mark does not want. Angélique would add posts to this ground with no plain surface to set them on.

findings.where: Hero: the amber hatch in the drawing's third arch and the amber 'Write to Mark' button; the palette's Sodium Amber swatch ('daylight in the drawing, and the one action')
findings.fault: The one contrasting hue has two jobs: it is decoration in the drawing and it also marks the only action. On the first screen, the amber-hatched arch and the amber button read as the same kind of thing, so the button's colour no longer singles out the one thing to do.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor scanning the hero. With amber in two places, it is less clear that the button is the one thing to act on, so amber stops meaning 'act here'.
